rubric.item: SPEC-16 correctness (E1-E7 exactly as approved, nothing loosened)
SPEC-17 correctness (both 10k runs exit 0, 0 violations, byte-identical reruns)

findings.issue: Nothing tests checkDeal's C5 returned-chips rule (src/engine/invariants.ts:493). That rule is the reason checkDeal exists for hands dealt out at the deal (A-6, §5). The `wrongReturn` case looks like it covers the rule, but checkState's conservation check already flags it, so the returnedMessage branch never decides the result.
findings.evidence: Mutation: replaced `? returnedMessage(state)` with `? null` in checkDeal. All 51 tests in check-deal, all-in-blinds, button-blinds and tests/playtest still pass. Probe: checkState(wrongReturn) returns [chips 'table holds $158 but the hand started with $161'] by itself. A case only C5 catches: W7 dealt-out state with result.returned = {seat:1, amount:3}, seat 1 stack +3 and seat 2 stack -3. checkState gives [] and checkDeal gives [chips 'seat 1 got $3 back but $0 was uncalled']. With the mutation, checkDeal gives [].
findings.fix: Replace the wrongReturn case (or add one beside it) with a state where conservation holds but the return is wrong. Example: W7 with `returned: {seat: 1, amount: 3}` and stacks moved +3 to seat 1 and -3 from seat 2. Assert checkState(state) is [] and checkDeal(state) equals [{invariant:'chips', message:'seat 1 got $3 back but $0 was uncalled'}].

findings.issue: The 'restart after a violating hand' check flags the first action, so every flagged hand also ends with final.result === null. The `hand.violations > 0` half of the restart condition (src/playtest/runner.ts:320) is never what triggers the restart. If a violation is flagged on the action that completes the hand, final.result is non-null and only that half restarts the table (A-3).
findings.evidence: Mutation: changed runner.ts:320 to `if (final.result === null) continue;`. The 'carried stacks and restarts' test still passes. The AC#9 seam case also restarts through result === null, because no actions are played.
findings.fix: Flag the step whose result completes the hand (step.result.ok && step.result.state.result !== null) on hand 1. Assert that hand 2 has button 1 and every seat at CASH_BUY_IN.

summary: The engine and runner changes match the spec. nextButton skips busted seats, wraps, and starts from a busted button. The blinds move with no dead or missed blind, and 3 -> 2 players gives a heads-up hand with the button on the small blind. All-in blinds keep amount = blind size and added = chips posted, with currentBet staying at the full big blind (D-1). bettingOver deals a hand out at the deal (D-2) and ends a round mid-hand (D-3). checkDeal puts the cross-hand message in the chips slot, in INVARIANTS order. Cash rebuys a busted seat, sng sits it out and restarts, and A-3 restarts the table after a violation. Replay word 2 is 0 for cash and 1 for sng, and the CLI text matches §5 exactly. Mutations that break D-2, D-3, the nextButton chip filter, the cross-hand seat union, the rebuy expectation, deal-violation counting, blind text, the per-hand policy, or passing `previous` all fail tests. One mutation-tested gap is MAJOR: checkDeal's C5 returned rule has no test that only it can satisfy. Fuzz runs: (1) 20,000 random small-stack hands at 2-10 seats with random policies gave clean checkDeal/checkStep, chips conserved, and no seat ever asked to act with nobody to bet against. (2) 12,000 runner hands (cash and sng, sizes 2/3/5/6/9, three seeds) gave 0 violations, and every hand replays bit-identically via playHand with the recorded stacks, button and game, including CLI --stacks replays. Both 10k seed-42 runs exit 0 with 0 violations, and their reruns are byte-identical. Deviations, judged on substance: E7 (bet-cap counts only REQ-016.5 counted bets) uses the same half-bet rule as the checker's independent countedBets. It still fails on a real 5th counted bet, and the line-233 optional chain can't hide a null, because undefined fails toMatch. Not loosened in substance. Q-6 (SPEC-10 >= 1 completed sit-and-go plus the next hand starting fresh at 1500 with button 1) still proves the AC#6 restart. The replaced cli.test.ts source-text check (violationBlock typed ViolatingHand, no '=== null') is out of date under D-7. The behaviour test that replaces it asserts the exact deal-violation lines and that 'player action' does not appear, so it is no weaker. E1-E6 are exactly as approved, and E5 is stricter. Size is 1,304 lines over 18 files against a budget of 1,250 lines and 16 files. The 2 extra files are the approved next-hand.test.ts floor change and E7, and nothing is out of scope.
